question: The force exerted by an object perpendicular to the surface is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**thrust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thrust is the force exerted by an object perpendicular to the surface on which it rests.
 
• This force is often considered in the context of fluids, but it applies to solids as well.
 
• Thrust is measured in Newtons (N), the standard unit of force.
 
• It is an important concept in physics and engineering, especially in the study of fluid dynamics and aerodynamics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weight**

 
 
• Weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object.
 
• It is calculated as the mass of the object multiplied by the acceleration due to gravity (9.8 m/s²).
 
 
 
• **Pressure**
 
 
• Pressure is defined as force per unit area.
 
• It is measured in Pascals (Pa).
 
 
 
• **Buoyancy**
 
 
• Buoyancy is the force exerted by a fluid that opposes an object's weight.
 
• This force allows objects to float in a fluid.
